When the planner places tests, it shall put each test whose weight is above the heavy threshold on a different shard before it fills the rest longest-first.
When a land run of quality-gates completes with the new placement, its total time shall be under 300 s.
The record shall report the measured total and slowest shard of one land run with 12 shards and one with 8 shards.
payload.description:
## Context
Measured 2026-11-20 on the last 15 land/* runs of quality-gates: total 211-340 s, 2 runs over the 5-minute CI rule. The pytest step per shard took 75-170 s although shard_weights.json plans about equal loads. The slowest shards hold the heaviest integration tests, which ran 1.6-1.8 times slower than their weights while 3 other xdist workers ran in the same job; in one run the two heaviest tests shared shard 12. In the same run a faulthandler "Timeout (0:01:00)!" stack dump fired inside landing_fingerprint in src/basicly/pytest_inputs.py while the two heavy tests ran, so a slow landing fingerprint is checked as a cause too. Placing each heavy test on its own shard first should bring the slowest shard near the heaviest test plus setup.

## Confirmation Plan
Run the shard placement unit tests, then one land run with 12 shards and one with 8, and read each run's slowest shard and total from gh run view.
payload.title: Place the heaviest ci tests one per shard before the longest-first fill

When a release run succeeds, the Tutorial walk shall have completed before Publish GitHub release started.
payload.description:
## Context
In release.yml the Tutorial walk job runs after Publish GitHub release. On v0.46.5 (2026-11-19) the release was published at 13:34:24 and the Tutorial walk then failed, so a published release had a red run. Running the walk before Publish lets a failing walk block publication.

## Confirmation Plan
Read release.yml needs edges, run the workflow check, and read the job order of the next release run with gh run view.
payload.title: Run the tutorial walk before the release is published

refine-sheet writes one sheet of the open records that miss criteria inside the git folder, and apply-sheet applies the filled sheet in one command, refusing the whole sheet and naming each empty or unknown id.
The definition of ready stays enforced: on the 20-issue beads sample, one filled sheet and one apply make every workable record ready (terminal baseline 2026-11-20: 0 of 19 ready).
apply-sheet reports the records it shaped and, separately, the records the scheduler lists as ready (terminal H1: 19 shaped, 16 ready).
An in_progress record with no holder is kept out of ready, and blocked lists it as in progress elsewhere with its start time and the claim command that adopts it (terminal H2, Orchestrator decision 2).

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
When the three heaviest tests are profiled, the record shall name where their time goes, per test, from the profile.
When a heavy test is changed, it shall keep every assertion of what it proves, and its runner time on a land run shall drop.
When a land run of quality-gates completes after the change, the slowest shard shall take less time than the 240 s measured before.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
Measured 2026-11-20: the shard planner already balances summed test weight (253 s per shard of 12), but 14 tests weigh over 40 s each, 873 s or 29% of the 3,037 s suite, in tests/test_kit_vault_hooks.py, test_integration_loop.py, test_integration_supervisor.py, test_repo_isolation.py, test_loop_cleanup_retry.py, test_claim_load.py, test_integration_supervisor_coupling.py, test_bulk_load.py and test_landing_anchors.py. On a land runner they run 1.6-1.8 times their weight under xdist contention (76.9 s against 41.8; 67.1 against 42.5; 109.3 against 63.9), and they set the floor of every shard: the slowest shards (pytest 161-170 s) hold two of them. A faulthandler "Timeout (0:01:00)!" dump fired inside landing_fingerprint in src/basicly/pytest_inputs.py during one of them, so a slow fingerprint is checked as a cause too. First step: profile the three heaviest with --durations and cProfile or py-spy and report where the time goes (git subprocesses, fixed sleeps, polling, real CI calls). A faster fixture that proves the same is in scope; a test that loses what it proves is not.

## Confirmation Plan
Profile the three heaviest tests, change only what the profile names, then compare each test's runner time on one land run before and after with gh run view.

payload.name: title
payload.value: Speed up the 14 heaviest integration tests without losing what they prove
